title: Urban Appraisal: Physiological Recording during Rating of Different Urban Environments
description: This dataset contains continuous EEG, ECG, and EDA recordings from 63 participants who viewed and rated Streetview images of urban environments across nine subjective scales (e.g., valence, safety, beauty). The study aims to investigate how urban environmental features influence subjective appraisal and neural responses such as stimulus-locked ERPs. Data were collected in 2024 at the BeMoBIL lab, TU Berlin.
methods_description: 64-channel EEG data were recorded using actively amplified wet electrodes in the 10-20 system referenced to FCz, along with ECG (right clavicle and left shinbone) and EDA (middle and ring fingers of the non-dominant hand) using BrainAmp DC amplifiers (BrainProducts GmbH). Data were sampled at 500 Hz with 16-bit resolution and a 0.016 Hz high-pass filter. Participants viewed 56 Streetview images and rated each on 9 scales across two blocks separated by a break, with EEG, ECG, and EDA recorded throughout.

funding_references.funder_name: This Study was realized by funding from the Berlin University Alliance.
